title: Water Legislation Amendment (Inspector-General of Water Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2021
short_title: Water Legislation Amendment (Inspector-General of Water Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2021

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create an independent Inspector-General of Water Compliance to oversee water law enforcement in the Murray-Darling Basin.
The Inspector-General, appointed by the Governor-General, would take over compliance and audit powers from the Murray-Darling Basin Authority and replace the interim inspector-general.
New criminal and civil penalties would target unlawful water taking and trading, with the Inspector-General required to notify state agencies before acting.
changes: Establishes the statutory role of Inspector-General of Water Compliance.
Transfers compliance, audit and assurance functions from the Murray-Darling Basin Authority to the Inspector-General.
Creates new offence and civil penalty provisions for unlawful water take and water rights trading.
summary.affected: Commonwealth and Basin State agencies managing Murray-Darling Basin water resources, and persons involved in water take or trading.

divisions.question: Water Legislation Amendment (Inspector-General of Water Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2021 - in Committee - Nationals' amendments

The majority voted against [amendments](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22legislation%2Famend%2Fr6721_amend_ece809ae-7028-4fa3-9762-ddc32fd223ac%22;rec=0) introduced by Victorian Senator and Leader of the Nationals in the Senate, Senator [Bridget McKenzie](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/victoria/bridget_mckenzie), which means the amendments failed. Interestingly, these amendments were inconsistent with the Cabinet's views, meaning that the Nationals were breaking with the rest of the Coalition in introducing them. ### What does this bill do? According to the [bill homepage](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/r6721), the bill was introduced to: > * *establish the role of an independent Inspector-General of Water Compliance to monitor, and provide independent oversight of, water compliance;* > * *provide for the Inspector-General's powers and functions; and* > * *introduce new offence and civil penalty provisions for unlawful conduct relating to the taking of water and new civil penalties for conduct relating to trading of water rights*
Water Legislation Amendment (Inspector-General of Water Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2021 - in Committee - Water register

The majority voted in favour of voting immediately on the [motion of dissent](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/divisions/senate/2021-06-24/17) moved by Queensland Senator [Larissa Waters](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/queensland/larissa_waters) (Greens), which means it succeeded.

The majority voted against a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2021-06-24.206.1) "*That the ruling of the President be dissented from*", which was introduced by Queensland Senator [Larissa Waters](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/queensland/larissa_waters) (Greens). This means it failed. ### What does this motion mean? Senator Waters is [opposing a ruling](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2021-06-24.201.1) by the President that "putting the question immediately means putting it immediately without debate."

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2021-06-24.208.1) to not insist on its amendments to the [Water Legislation Amendment (Inspector-General of Water Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2021](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/r6721). This means that the bill can be passed and become law. ### What does this bill do? According to the [bill homepage](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/r6721), the bill was introduced to: > * *establish the role of an independent Inspector-General of Water Compliance to monitor, and provide independent oversight of, water compliance;* > * *provide for the Inspector-General's powers and functions; and* > * *introduce new offence and civil penalty provisions for unlawful conduct relating to the taking of water and new civil penalties for conduct relating to trading of water rights*

speeches.speaker: Terri Butler
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Coalition Government has bungled the Murray-Darling Basin Plan’s implementation and abandoned its targets, while supporting the bill to create a statutory Inspector-General of Water Compliance. They noted only 1.9 of the required 450 gigalitres of additional water has been delivered, criticised repeated delays and broken commitments on oversight roles, and urged swift state approvals and stronger action on water market reforms.

speeches.speaker: Damian Drum
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Murray-Darling Basin Plan has damaged communities and agriculture, and supported the creation of an Inspector-General of Water Compliance to improve accountability. He opposed further water recovery, particularly the additional 450 gigalitres, and criticised Labor’s policy of water buybacks, stating that $500 million per year in productivity is lost from the Goulburn Valley alone.

speeches.speaker: Tony Zappia
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Water Legislation Amendment Bill 2021, which creates the Office of the Inspector-General of Water Compliance, but argued it acknowledges the Murray-Darling Basin Authority's failures, noting only 1.9 of the promised 450 gigalitres of environmental water has been delivered and calling for implementation of the South Australian royal commission's 44 recommendations to address ongoing state disputes, illegal water taking, and market speculation.

speeches.speaker: Angus Taylor
speeches.brief: The government is delivering strong leadership and confidence in compliance and enforcement institutions for the Murray-Darling Basin through the Water Legislation Amendment (Inspector-General of Water Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2021.

speeches.speaker: Alicia Payne
speeches.brief: The Labor member supported the Water Legislation Amendment Bill 2021, which establishes an inspector-general of water compliance with new penalties including fines up to $1.1 million for individuals and $11 million for companies, but criticised the Morrison government for delaying reforms and failing to address the Murray-Darling Basin's ecological and cultural crisis, including the impacts of climate change and the need for First Nations involvement in water management.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Water Legislation Amendment (Inspector-General of Water Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2021 is necessary to secure water trading integrity, criticising the government for acquiring only 2.1 of the planned 450 gigalitres of environmental water and failing to deliver infrastructure funding to irrigators, which harms both communities and river health. They also stated that removing the cap on buybacks eliminated states’ incentives to complete water-saving projects, worsening the plan's implementation.
